A day for each feast

Lunar New Year (Chunjie)

A Joyful Lunar New Year at Home

Welcome the Lunar New Year, a time-honored festival rooted in ancient agrarian cycles, symbolizing the arrival of spring and new beginnings. This day is dedicated to family reunions, ancestor veneration, and setting intentions for a prosperous year ahead.

  1. Early Morning

    Spring Cleaning & Decorating

    Begin the day by thoroughly cleaning your home, a symbolic act of sweeping away any lingering bad luck from the past year. Afterward, adorn your living space with vibrant red decorations and lanterns to invite joy and good fortune.

  2. Late Morning

    Crafting Ingots of Fortune

    Gather the family to make dumplings together. Their shape resembles ancient gold ingots, symbolizing wealth and prosperity for the coming year. It's a wonderful bonding activity!

    Recipes: Chinese Pork and Cabbage Dumplings (Jiaozi)

  3. Lunch

    A Simple Midday Meal

    Enjoy a light and simple lunch, reserving your appetite for the grand reunion banquet later in the evening. This allows time for continued preparations and relaxation.

  4. Afternoon

    Sharing Blessings & Abundance

    Exchange red envelopes (hongbao) with blessings for prosperity and good fortune. Share and enjoy mandarin oranges, which symbolize abundance and good luck due to their golden color.

    Recipes: Festive Mandarin Orange Presentation

  5. Late Afternoon

    Preparing the Reunion Feast

    Begin the preparations for the most important meal of the year. Focus on dishes that carry auspicious meanings, such as whole fish for abundance and longevity noodles for a long life.

    Recipes: Longevity Noodles with Pork and Vegetables · Steamed Whole Fish for Lunar New Year

  6. Evening

    The Reunion Banquet

    Gather around the table for the traditional reunion dinner, a cornerstone of Lunar New Year celebrations. Share the meticulously prepared dishes, symbolizing family unity, prosperity, and good health for all.

    Recipes: Longevity Noodles with Pork and Vegetables · Steamed Whole Fish for Lunar New Year · Chinese Pork and Cabbage Dumplings (Jiaozi)

  7. Late Evening

    Sweet Endings

    Conclude your festive day by enjoying sweet rice cakes (Nian Gao). This traditional dessert symbolizes a 'higher year' of growth and prosperity, wishing everyone a sweet and successful new beginning.

    Recipes: Sweet Lunar New Year Rice Cakes (Nian Gao)

May your home be filled with joy, prosperity, and good fortune throughout the new year!
